alex: Hey — noticed a big LCP/heatmap slow spike in EU canary after yesterday's splitpoint asset priority tweak. Charts hang for ~400-800ms on first interaction :eyes:
maya: ugh. link to telemetry?
alex: https://console/reports/heatmap?canary=eu — 95th went from 120ms -> 540ms after the splitpoint roll. main-thread parse and module eval are spiking.
linh: I think the kvcache TTL we lowered for aggressive eviction during the bundle-split rollout is causing repeated prefix misses for heatmap tiles. I saw a lot more "kv-prefetch miss" events.
sam: can you paste the config?
linh: snippet: `KVCACHE_TTL_MS=30000 -> 5000` and `SPLITPOINT_PRIORITY=lazy` in the canary manifest. we did this to reduce memory but may have been too aggressive.
carol: we also changed import order so the heatmap worker bundle moves behind shared-chunk B. that increases parse cost on first paint.
maya: so two factors: 1) smaller TTL -> more kv misses, 2) asset priority moved -> increased main-thread work. both amplify first-interaction latency.
alex: exact observed stack:
```
main-thread: parse shared-chunk-B (42ms) -> eval heatmap-worker stub (18ms) -> fetch tile (120ms network) -> kv-prefetch miss -> decompress (blocking)
```
maya: can we test bumping ttl back in canary without touching splitpoint priority? quick A/B.
linh: I can patch TTL to 30s in canary and re-run. If that fixes it, we know kvcache is dominant.
sam: if TTL bump fixes most of it, we should consider making splitpoint priority opt-in by route: heatmap routes get higher inline priority. default splitpoint remains lazy.
carol: agree — heatmap is a high-LCP route so special-casing seems fine. we should also consider prefetch hints for its small worker chunk.
alex: can we also add a telemetry gauge for "kvcache-miss-rate by route"? right now it's noisy to query.
maya: yes — I'll add a dashboard tile with a kvcache miss-rate KPI and 95th main-thread parse time per route. Should help catch regressions.
linh: patching TTL now, will post deploy link.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy started: https://ci.redwood/rollouts/314159 — triggered by linh.
carol: quick note — if we bump TTL we might increase memory usage on canary GPUs for prefix cache. monitor kvcache memory and evictions.
sam: can we do dynamic per-route TTL? heatmap routes 30s, low-priority routes 5s. avoids global rollback.
linh: technically doable; need small infra change to attach TTL metadata to route keys. I'll spike it tomorrow.
alex: OK let's wait on TTL canary results first. if good, we'll: 1) revert TTL change in prod rollout, 2) add per-route TTL, 3) consider raising priority for heatmap splitpoint or prefetching its worker.
maya: adding ticket for dashboard + runbook entry: "Investigate heatmap LCP regression post-splitpoint" and linking this thread.
sam: :thumbsup: thanks folks — appreciate the quick triage.
linh: deployed TTL bump complete, canary link: https://ci.redwood/rollouts/314159/status — will follow up in ~10m with telemetry snapshots.
alex: thanks. ping me if 95th doesn't drop below 200ms.
maya: noted — adding alerts for kvcache-miss-rate > 2% and main-thread-parse 95th > 300ms for heatmap route.
carol: once stable we should document tradeoffs for splitpoint priority vs cache TTL in the rollout checklist. saved me a headache :)
alex: agreed.
